title: Physical Activity for Kids in NZ – Family Gym Options & Tips
meta_desc: Discover NZ guidelines for children's activity, family-friendly gyms, YMCA swimming, crèche and holiday programmes. Practical steps to keep kids moving.
intro: Getting kids active is a top priority for New Zealand families. This guide outlines national recommendations, real‑world gym options and easy steps to make movement a daily habit for the whole family.

sections.heading: What the NZ Guidelines Say
sections.body: The Ministry of Health recommends that children aged 5‑17 get at least 60 minutes of moderate‑to‑vigorous physical activity each day, with a mix of aerobic, strength and flexibility work. Short bursts throughout the day count – a 10‑minute game of tag or a quick bike ride adds up. The guidelines also stress limiting sedentary screen time to under two hours daily.

sections.heading: Why It Matters – NZ Child Activity Stats
sections.body: Recent NZ Health Survey data shows only 41% of 5‑14 year‑olds meet the daily activity target, while 30% exceed recommended screen time. Low activity levels are linked to rising childhood obesity rates – currently 11% of primary school kids are classified as obese. Regular movement improves mental health, academic performance and reduces future chronic disease risk.

sections.heading: YMCA Swimming, Crèche & Holiday Programmes
sections.body: YMCA clubs are the most comprehensive option for families with young children. All major centres offer supervised swimming sessions, a on‑site crèche (often included in the family membership) and holiday camps that blend sport, arts and NZ cultural activities. Prices for holiday camps run $150‑$250 per week per child, with discounts for existing members.

sections.heading: Practical Steps & Using the Exercise NZ Subsidised Scheme
sections.body: The Exercise NZ programme offers eligible families 40‑70% off standard gym fees. To qualify, check your health board’s eligibility list and apply online. Once you have a subsidised membership, use it to schedule regular family workouts – a 30‑minute circuit, a swim class, or a weekend hike. Set a weekly family activity calendar, involve kids in planning, and celebrate milestones with non‑food rewards.
list: Book a free family induction session at your chosen gym.
Create a simple calendar: e.g., Monday swim, Wednesday family HIIT, Saturday park run.
